newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe stocks advance further in active market.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe stocks advance further in active market.

text.p: Zimbabwe's Stock Exchange hit a new record on Wednesday, rising 1.8 percent as investors continued to relish forecasts of gross domestic product growth of seven percent in 1997 on the back of good rains.
The main 57-share industrial index soared 161.20 points to end at a new all time high of 9,291.88.
"Now it's difficult to say when the market will correct," said one broker who, with others earlier this week had predicted a price correction next week.
"The only thing we can say is it's inevitable that it will come down at some point," he added.
Another trader said the market was short of scrip which indicated people believed that prices could be chased higher.
"Although the prices are high they are not inducing any selling. If there are more sellers than buyers then we will get a correction," he said.

Among Wednesday's winners, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans leapt 200 cents to 5,000, farming implement-maker Zimplow surged 140 cents to 610, finance group Finhold, blue-chip beverages and supermarket conglomerate Delta and bankers Barclays each jumped 100 cents to 850, 4,000 and 2,900 respectively.
Clothing and furniture group Tedco rose 80 cents to 1,200, clothing retailer Truworths gained 50 cents to 1,250 as did sugar producer Hippo at 1,150 and transport group Clan at 510.

Tobacco firm TSL added 35 cents to 775, steel windows and door manufacturer Radar at 390 and tyre re-processor NTS at 500 both put on 30 cents, while cement producer Porthold and sugar refinery ZSR each traded 25 cents up at 1,450 and 1,500 respectively.
Against the trend, hotel and supermarket group Meikles dropped 200 cents to 2,000 and food and hotel conglomerate TA shed 10 cents to 165.
In minings, Wankie Colliery pared off overnight gains, trading five cents easier at 630 but nickel producer Bindura rose 40 cents to 860.
The seven-counter mining index gained 11.02 points to 1,135.19.
